plan.hero_lede: A ward gets better the way a runner gets faster: a clear goal, a plan you can follow, and honest splits along the way. Here is what Shakedia Jones will work on for the 1st Ward, and how she will report back to you.
plan.index_aria: Jump to a lane of the plan

l1.name: Safe neighborhoods
l1.why_1: The 1st Ward stretches along the lakefront, home to Washington, Roosevelt, King, Kirk, Smith, Woodard, Besley and Bedrosian parks. Those parks should be the safest places in the neighborhood.
l1.why_2: Families want their kids to be safe walking to school and playing in the park. Safety starts with neighbors who know each other and a city that works with them.
l1.c1: Lead regular ward walks with neighbors and partner with block clubs, so concerns travel straight from the block to City Hall.
l1.c2: Push the city, and work with the Park District, for better lighting and safety upgrades in 1st Ward parks and on the streets around them, starting where neighbors say they feel least safe.
l1.c3: Bring residents, police, park staff and community groups to the same table at ward meetings, so safety plans are made with the neighborhood, not for it.
l1.c4: Follow up on every safety concern a neighbor raises, and report back on what the city did about it.

l2.name: Youth programming
l2.title_2: a shot at their own finish line.
l2.why_1: Nearly one in four Waukegan residents is under 18. Growing up, Shakedia's family could not pay for organized sports until high school. A cousin talked her into going out for track, and it changed her life.
l2.why_2: Too many 1st Ward kids still sit out because of a fee, a ride or a locked door. She has spent her career opening those doors, and she wants the ward to open more.
l2.c1: Work with the Waukegan Park District to keep park and Smith recreation center programs open later in the summer.
l2.c2: Connect families to fee help for sports, arts and camps, so cost is less often the reason a kid sits out.
l2.c3: Bring coaches, mentors, schools and local businesses together to grow youth programs in the ward.
l2.c4: Hold youth listening sessions, so young people help decide what the ward fights for.
l2.record_1: Founded Furthering the Lives of Youth (FLY) in 2014. More than 600 young people helped (her 2024 count).
l2.record_2: Has coached the Waukegan High School girls track team.
l2.photo_alt: A large group of kids and adults gathered outside an arena at dusk.
l2.photo_caption: A summer outing with Waukegan kids, 2026.
l2.record_note: Furthering the Lives of Youth is a nonprofit organization. It is separate from this campaign and does not endorse candidates.

l3.name: Strong infrastructure
l3.title_2: and lead lines replaced on schedule.
l3.why_1: The city's 2026 budget sets aside $30.6 million for streets, sidewalks and alleys. 1st Ward neighbors deserve to know where the work is happening and when.
l3.why_2: State-required lead service line replacement begins by January 2027, and it is free to residents. Every family should know when their block is up and what to expect.
l3.c1: Share the city's lead service line replacement schedule by block, in English and Spanish, so every household knows what to expect and that the work is free.
l3.c2: Help neighbors report broken sidewalks, potholes and alley problems through the city, and track each report until it is fixed.
l3.c3: Push for a clear, public list of planned street, sidewalk and alley work in the 1st Ward.
l3.c4: Walk the ward with city staff to move the worst spots to the front of the line.

l4.name: Transparent government
l4.why_1: More than half of Waukegan residents speak a language other than English at home. City government should be easy to follow and easy to reach, in both languages.
l4.why_2: Trust is built the way races are won: in the open, one split at a time.
l4.c1: Hold regular ward meetings in English and Spanish, at times and places working families can make.
l4.c2: Post how she votes on major council decisions and explain why, in plain language.
l4.c3: Publish a simple monthly ward report: what she worked on, what got fixed, and what is still open.
l4.c4: Answer neighbors directly and follow up on every call and message.

plan.how_lede: Champions are built on discipline, not luck. Shakedia pairs a coach's training plan with an MBA from Keller Graduate School of Management and more than ten years running a nonprofit. That is the approach she will bring to the 1st Ward.

how.s1_text: At the park, the block club and the ward meeting. You cannot coach from the bleachers.
how.s2_text: Agree with neighbors on what winning looks like, block by block.
how.s3_text: Turn every goal into clear steps and dates, with the same discipline it takes to run a nonprofit and a training season.
how.s4_text: Report back every month: what moved, what stalled, and what comes next.

plan.quote: I tell them whatever it is you do, make it your Olympics.
plan.quote_context: It is what she tells young people. It is also the standard she will hold herself to in the 1st Ward.
plan.cta_text: Help put Shakedia on the ballot and knock doors in the 1st Ward, or tell her what your block needs most.
